definition: An equation $\boldsymbol{r} = \boldsymbol{a} + \lambda\boldsymbol{b}$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$, that gives the position vector $\boldsymbol{r}$ of every point on a line from the position vector $\boldsymbol{a}$ of one known point and a direction vector $\boldsymbol{b}$.
A non-zero vector parallel to a line, so that any non-zero multiple of it is also a direction vector of the same line.
The equations $x = x_{0} + \lambda l$, $y = y_{0} + \lambda m$, $z = z_{0} + \lambda n$, which give each coordinate of a point on a line in terms of the parameter $\lambda$.

The equations $\frac{x - x_{0}}{l} = \frac{y - y_{0}}{m} = \frac{z - z_{0}}{n}$ of the line through $(x_{0}, y_{0}, z_{0})$ with direction $\begin{pmatrix}l\\m\\n\end{pmatrix}$, found by removing $\lambda$ from the parametric equations.

The acute or right angle between two lines, found from their direction vectors by $\cos\theta = \frac{\lvert\boldsymbol{b}_1 \cdot \boldsymbol{b}_2\rvert}{\lvert\boldsymbol{b}_1\rvert\lvert\boldsymbol{b}_2\rvert}$.
